title: ID0477929-DC/Si-D/AT- [Multi] Resistance dropped below 500kOhm during plug-in leads to session failure
description:
Reported behavior/issue: Resistance dropped below 500kOhm during plug-in leads to session failure
The customer reports that his Jaguar I‑Pace cannot charge at several OMV sites using our Sicharge D chargers, although  charging works normally at Alpitronic and other stations. Authentication was always successful, but the charging process  borted during the handshake after about 15 seconds, showing “Out of service” on the charger and “Charging not possible” in  he car. Affected locations and charger IDs:
• 24 Jan, ~13:10 – OMV Bad Fischau, chargers MP/S7170003960 or MP/S8170003941
• 14 Jan, 08:20 – OMV Wienerstraße 126, 2700 Wiener Neustadt, chargers RVP/T7170004901 or RVP/T7170004900, system ATOMVEA8672DC6117
• 23 Dec – same Wiener Neustadt site, chargers RVP/T7170004900 or RVP/T7170004901
On Dec 23 the charging attempt caused a full vehicle crash requiring ÖAMTC support. Jaguar confirmed the car is fully
functional, and the customer charged successfully at many other stations. A qualified technical assessment is urgently needed for OMV
Fleet analysis for “Insulation resistance dropped” was suggested; however this can be tricky since the Insulation resistance dropped could be logged also in other charging phases after Cable Check - which is not the scope of this ticket
Solution: Update vo 10.X

additional_info.subject: Log collection on 2hSn7C
additional_info.body:
Analysis on MP/S7170003960 (ID: 2hSn7C);
Vehicle charging EVMAC: "9c.f6.dd.91.bb.0c\"
Reported Insulation resistance below alarm level: 1kOhm at 11:33. Insulation level is logged after the charger already stopped the charging, however the DC output contactors are still closed at the time of fault and pilot state is C2, hence the IMD is still measuring the vehicle impedance as the vehicle is still connected.
As further confirmation, the same ISO reading happens when the output contactors open while the vehicle is still connected (visible from pilot state B2). This confirms that the EV has an Insulation value below norm.
The reading of IMD is reported less than 1s later:

additional_info.subject: Log collection on t3PbfN
additional_info.body: Issue not spotted on MP/S8170003941 (ID: t3PbfN); no IMD deviations nor charging sessions in the reported timestamp

additional_info.subject: Log collection on q92B3d
additional_info.body: Issue not spotted on RVP/T7170004900 (ID: q92B3d); no IMD deviations in the reported timestamp; spotted a charging session which did not show any error and proceeded correctly for 37 minutes.

additional_info.subject: Log collection of K84Wd9
additional_info.body:
14 Jan 8:20 - Failed during plug in for EVMAC:
00.1a.37.71.25.fb

additional_info.subject: To be verified
additional_info.body:
In the case of 14 Jan 8:20 on charger K84Wd9, the session Failed during plug in for EVMAC:00.1a.37.71.25.fb.
The error reported is DC2: insulation resistance dropped: 483kOhm.
Although this is below warning level, it is above alarm level.
As per the norm: IEC 61851-23:2014-03
Chapter 6.4.3.106 Insulation test before charging - it defines the measures for a test with closed relays in the outputs, which for SiD is the cable check. Hence this chapter doesn't apply, and the rule of  R ≥ 100 Ω/V × U does not apply either, since for this very case the relays are still open (plugging in phase).
Chapter: CC.4 Safety measures , subchapter: CC.4.1 IT (isolated terra) system requirements:
Warning state: If the actual total physical insulation resistance between DC+/DC- to PE
falls below a value calculated by 500 Ω/V multiplied by the maximum output voltage rating
of the d.c. EV charging station (without negative tolerance) the d.c. supply shall send a
Warning message and store the Warning.
In the reported case, the 483kOhm is triggering the warning state which sets the charger out of order until a next successful IMD check, although this is not explicitly required in the norm for situations before power delivery.
It will be verified with R&D on ticket TS2RD-62 why this acknowledged warning state is causing a charging stop.

additional_info.subject: ID0477929-DC/Si-D/AT- [Multi] Sicharge Interoperability Conflict CRM:03289000545
additional_info.body:
Hi Johannes,
Here is our analysis for the several chargers and timestamps, I will start with the easier ones and leave the most difficult to the end:
1. Issue not spotted on RVP/T7170004900 (ID: q92B3d); no IMD deviations in the reported timestamp; spotted a charging session which did not show any error and proceeded correctly for 37 minutes on the 14th Jan.
2. Issue not spotted on MP/S8170003941 (ID: t3PbfN); no IMD deviations nor charging sessions in the reported timestamp on the 24th Jan.
3. Analysis on MP/S7170003960 (ID: 2hSn7C); Vehicle charging EVMAC: "9c.f6.dd.91.bb.0c"
Reported Insulation resistance below alarm level: 1kOhm at 11:33. Insulation level is logged after the charger already stopped the charging, however the DC output contactors are still closed at the time of fault and pilot state is C2, hence the IMD is still measuring the vehicle impedance as the vehicle is still connected.
As further confirmation, the same ISO reading happens when the output contactors open while the vehicle is still connected (visible from pilot state B2). This confirms that the EV has an Insulation value below norm.
The reading of IMD is reported less than 1s later:
4.
Log collection of K84Wd9: 23 December -
"EVMAC":
"44.1d.b1.b1.87.35".
As you can see this behavior is the same as shown above except that instead of happening in the P06_Charge it is during P03_Cable_Check
According to the IEC-61851-23 (2014):
With a U = 1000V, the minimum Resistance value is 100kOhm
Also confirmed in the "normal start-up" for a session:
In this norm it's also specified what to do in case we find a Resistance < 100kOhm:
As such, it's more than clear that every fail during Cable Check or afterwards where the resistance drops below 100kOhm it's EV fault. Also confirmed in the norm that:
In these cases, after the EV is unplugged, the charger is back to available, which means that the self-test was successful.
Now for the most difficult case,
14 Jan 8:20 - Failed during plug in for EVMAC:
00.1a.37.71.25.fb
In this case after plug-in we have a drop below 500kOhm (483kOhm) but indeed, in the norm, it does not mention that we should abort the session:
But it does mention this:
From what we understand, there is a defined fault resistor, but it doesn't have a defined value, it's like everyone can decide their own. This is where we believe our difference is between SiD and Alpi, they most likely defined this value to be lower and are able to go through with the session.
We already opened a ticket to understand the reason why we choose this value.
As soon as we have a reply from R&D, we will convey it to you.
Thank you very much for your patience and understanding.
Best regards,
Francisco
